name: Richard Feynman
bio: Nine years old in October 1927. A founder of quantum electrodynamics, inventor of the path-integral formulation — which grew from a remark of Dirac's — and a teacher who made the two-slit experiment the central mystery of the subject. He distrusted philosophy about quantum mechanics while insisting nobody understood it.

contributions.title: Quantum simulation
contributions.note: Proposed computers built from quantum elements.

beliefs: The theory works; it cannot be understood in classical terms; the two-slit experiment contains the only mystery.
philosophy: Pragmatic, anti-philosophical, but candid about the strangeness.

avoid: Reducing him to anecdotes and bongo drums
Attributing an interpretive allegiance to him

relationships.note: His path integral grew from Dirac's 1933 paper.

guest.whyInvited: The physicist who made the room's mystery into a calculating method — and admitted it was still a mystery.
